item.title: New high-speed rail lines weave a denser network, boosting travel and regional growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
A drone photo taken on Sept. 28, 2026 shows the first train of Harbin-Yichun high-speed railway running in Yichun, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. (Xinhua/Wang Song)
BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- For Zhang Xintong, a resident of Harbin, capital city of northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, this National Day holiday was supposed to be a quiet break at home. But a newly opened high-speed rail line gave her the idea of a trip to Yichun, where she pictured herself in endless green forests and fresh air.
The new line, China's northernmost high-speed railway, links Harbin with Yichun, a popular summer retreat and forest tourism destination in the same province, along a 318-kilometer route. It officially entered service on Sept. 28, cutting railway travel time between the two cities from about seven hours to roughly two hours.
"Every seat was taken, and some passengers sat on folding chairs and stools in the corner," Zhang said of her Oct. 1 train journey. On board were business travelers, families returning to their hometowns, and friendly locals sharing travel tips with visitors.
This railway underlines the country's efforts to direct more transport infrastructure investment toward border areas, forest regions and less-developed regions, while helping boost development and prosperity in northeast China's border regions, said China Railway Harbin Group Co., Ltd.
Nationwide, China has already built the world's largest high-speed railway network and continues to weave a denser one, aiming to make travel more convenient, offer more tourism options, and promote coordinated regional development.
Also on Sept. 28, China opened three other high-speed rail sections, connecting Xiong'an in Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province, and Yichang with Xingshan in Hubei Province.
Ankang, in the mountainous area of southern Shaanxi, is rich in ecological resources. With the Xi'an-Ankang high-speed railway now in service, travel time between the two cities has been cut from three hours to as short as 45 minutes.
For Qu Xiaoyuan, an Ankang cultural and tourism official, the new line hit home. His brother, who works in Xi'an, called him the day it opened, joking that he could dash home to Ankang for dinner if the family cooked something delicious and still be back in Xi'an that night. "Cities are much closer now, not just on the map but in everyday life," Qu said.
As the new lines draw passengers from a wider area, weekend and short-holiday tourists may increase significantly, driving demand for multi-purpose and experience-oriented tourism products, Qu said. In response, tourist attractions will emphasize their unique features and focus on improving quality to avoid offering similar, copycat experiences.
Further east, the Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway line brings cities like Wuhan, Zhengzhou and Chongqing within two hours of Xingshan, weaving the Three Gorges, dense forests and cloud-kissed peaks scattered along the route into easy, spontaneous trips.
Beyond driving tourist trips, these newly opened lines are also boosting the flow of talent, technology and capital across regions.
Ma Botao, of the China Railway Economic Planning and Research Institute, said the expanding network is bringing cities and city clusters much closer together. Commuting within metropolitan areas now takes about one hour, living and working across city clusters about two hours, and business travel between neighboring city clusters and provincial capitals around three hours.
"The railway network closely binds large and small cities, making industrial division of labor and cross-city employment the norm," he said.
Noting that the Xiong'an-Shangqiu section fills a gap in Xiong'an New Area's southbound high-speed rail corridor, Liu Yanhong, deputy general manager of Xiong'an high-speed railway corporation, said the line facilitates commuting and business exchanges for relocated enterprises and institutions and supports stronger industrial cooperation along the route.
For cities newly connected to the network, seizing the opportunity depends on how well they position themselves.
"Generally, large cities focus on research and development, finance and headquarters economy, while small cities should leverage their local agriculture, ecology, tourism and distinctive industrial strengths to undertake supporting manufacturing, agricultural product processing, and wellness and cultural tourism, serving as both industrial supporting bases and leisure backyards for central cities," Ma said.
To turn transport advantages into real development gains, Ma advised cities to strengthen connections between high-speed rail stations and industrial parks as well as major population clusters, and improve housing and public services for talent.
Behind these expectations lies a network that keeps growing. By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
Fixed-asset investment in the railway sector totaled 511.8 billion yuan (about 76 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of the year, up 1.5 percent year on year, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd.
Under national plans, China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, with eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones throughout the country.

item.title: Why global travelers flock to China with empty suitcases
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
* With "China Haul" emerging as a buzz hashtag on social media platforms worldwide, more foreign visitors are flocking to the country not merely for sightseeing, but also for shopping sprees.
* In the first seven months of 2026, people from overseas spent 263.6 billion yuan (about 39 billion U.S. dollars) in China, an increase of 27.8 percent year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
* Official data showed that foreign nationals made almost 61.29 million border crossings in the January-August period of 2026, up 19.5 percent from a year earlier. Visa-free entries accounted for 23.72 million of the total, an increase of 26.8 percent compared with 2025.
BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- Andrea Triboldi, an Italian tourist, arrived in China with a long shopping list.
After landing in Shenzhen, a thriving tech hub in southern China, Triboldi and his 11-year-old son couldn't wait to visit a major sci-tech exhibition, which showcased drones and other latest tech products of this city in Guangdong Province.
Foreign tourists buy handheld camera equipment at a flagship store of DJI in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, June 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
Prior to the trip, Triboldi had drawn up a shopping list featuring more than 20 Chinese products. "I chose Shenzhen as the first station of our China travel because of its technology. My son is particularly into DJI drones and wants to buy one to take home," he said.
Triboldi is not alone. With "China Haul" emerging as a buzz hashtag on social media platforms worldwide, more foreign visitors are flocking to the country not merely for sightseeing, but also for shopping sprees.
DIVERSE SHOPPING SPREES
"I came here to feel the best technology I have ever seen in the whole world. It's really amazing. We don't have these kinds of drones in Mexico," said Ulises Padilla, an 11-year-old Mexican tourist, in describing his impressions of Shenzhen.
The city is drawing an increasing number of foreign visitors like Padilla. An average of nearly 8,000 foreign buyers have visited Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's mega electronics marketplace, each day this year. From January through July, sales of artificial intelligence (AI) products surged more than 55 percent from a year earlier in this area. Sales of AI glasses doubled, while sales of drones and robots climbed by 60 to 70 percent during the same period.
Tourists from the Republic of Korea experience AI translator at Huaqiangbei of Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, June 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
Zhang Linwan, an employee of INNO100, a Shenzhen store featuring tech products, said that foreign tourists contribute roughly 40 percent of the store's total sales.
"They show strong interest in exoskeletons, 3D printers and laser engraving machines. At our store, they can also make their own 3D dolls and turn photos of themselves and their families into fridge magnets," the employee added.
Foreign tourists experience AI sports glasses at an INNO100 shop in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Aug. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
Wang Linlin, who works at a DJI flagship store in Shenzhen, described a similar scene. "We've seen a large number of foreign customers recently. They enjoy getting hands-on experience with our products, especially trying out our drones in test flights," Wang revealed.
In Changsha, capital of central China's Hunan Province, Chinese snacks are proving a big hit with foreign tourists. Ivan, a 32-year-old Russian tourist, made a point of visiting Snack Kingdom, a specialty store in the city that offers over 35,000 types of snacks.
He said that not many large snack stores in Russia have such a complete range of products, and the variety is so rich that it's a bit difficult to choose.
Tanzanian tourist Shija Theodora Desderi commented that the store serves not only as a shopping destination but also as a place for entertainment. She compared Chinese snacks with Tanzanian ones, which she described as sweeter, noting that the former taste refreshing and are more organic, containing less sugar and salt.
"From sneakers and cosmetics to trendy toys and daily necessities, my family and friends often have their shopping plans ready before visiting China," said Mok Jin Jin from Malaysia.
She said her mother especially likes a Chinese-made blender and often uses it to make various healthy drinks for the family. The machine's one-touch automatic cleaning feature is particularly appealing, sparing her the hassle of manual cleaning.
APPEALING PRODUCTS PLUS FAVORABLE POLICIES
It is not only the price advantage, but the design, quality and practicality of Chinese products that draw the attention of foreign tourists, according to the Malaysian.
She concluded that behind the "China Haul" phenomenon lies not only China's enhanced manufacturing capabilities, but also profound shifts in Chinese brand design, innovation and consumer experience.
Carlos Alvarado, an international student from Guatemala, is already a seasoned shopper in China. "Chinese products, like clothes, accessories and daily necessities, are not only competitively priced, but also feature trendy designs that are hard to find in stores in my home country," he said.
Moreover, an array of favorable policies, such as visa-free policies and departure tax refunds, has further boosted the shopping frenzy in China.
A tourist from Mexico purchases shoes at an international smallware wholesale market in Yuzhong District of Chongqing, southwest China, April 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Wei)
Before ending her trip to Chengdu, capital city of southwest China's Sichuan Province, Hungarian tourist Annamaria purchased some tea, teacups and teapots as gifts for her mother and younger brother at home.
"I like shopping in China because it's very convenient and there are many choices here," she said, praising the tax refund policy for allowing her to get refunds immediately upon purchase.
"The policy has boosted our sales. Foreign tourists now account for 30 percent of our daily customer flow," said Zhou Man, manager of a Chengdu store of Xiaomi, a Chinese consumer electronics and technology company.
Data from the Ministry of Commerce revealed that the number of overseas visitors applying for departure tax refunds had increased by more than threefold year on year during the first seven months of 2026.
Roger Matute, an international student from Honduras, was impressed by how convenient mobile payment is in China. "I have rarely used cash since I arrived here because it is very easy to pay everything with my smartphone using WeChat or Alipay apps," he said.
Tourists from Russia have tea drinks in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Sept. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Zongzhi)
A range of favorable conditions, including tax refunds, mobile payments and visa-free policies, have systematically reduced the cost of cross-border consumer transactions, helping to facilitate the "China Haul" trend, according to Gao Li, vice dean of the School of International Business, Tianjin Foreign Studies University, located in north China.
The popularity of "China Haul" essentially stems from a shift in the consumption logic of overseas tourists, who are moving from purchasing foreign cultural symbols to buying Chinese technologies, designs and consumption experiences, said He Yun, an associate professor at the school of public administration of central China's Hunan University.
The trend, she noted, is underpinned by the upgrading of China's manufacturing and cultural and creative industries, a substantial transition from exporting production capacity to exporting brands and lifestyles.

item.title: Across China: 90 years on, Long March stories resonate across generations and borders
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
GUIYANG, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- Standing before a grave marked "Red Army Tomb" in Zunyi, a city in southwest China's Guizhou Province, Kong Xia told visitors about the young medic buried beneath it.
The medic was only 18 years old in January 1935, when the Red Army reached Zunyi during the Long March. Staying behind to treat sick villagers, he lost contact with his unit and was killed by enemy forces. Local people, risking their own lives, secretly buried the body.
A foreign listener once told her before the tomb: "A good deed is remembered, even a hundred years later."
For Kong Xia, a 56-year-old volunteer who has told Long March stories for more than three decades, the words capture something universal. The feelings the Long March evokes -- kindness, perseverance, longing for a good life -- belong to no single language or nation. Ninety years after the epic journey, the stories are finding new listeners and inspiring people in their everyday lives.
The Red Army, led by the Communist Party of China (CPC), was mainly made up of soldiers from peasants' and workers' families during the Chinese revolution. Between 1934 and 1936, the army trekked up to 12,500 kilometers to break through the Kuomintang party (KMT) siege, a journey later known as the Long March.
It was no easy journey. The army went through more than 600 battles while braving raging rivers, snow-covered mountains, and treacherous grasslands, with many dying on the way. By December 1934, less than two months into the march, the Central Red Army had lost more than half its strength, shrinking from over 86,000 to just over 30,000.
Known as China's "city of historic turning point," Zunyi holds a special place in the nation's history. In January 1935, after arriving, the CPC convened a three-day meeting to draw lessons from the loss, which ultimately corrected the army's strategic mistakes and established a new Party leadership with Mao Zedong at the helm.
About a month later, the Red Army won its first major victory of the march at Loushan Pass in Zunyi, proving the new strategy was working. The foundation laid in the mountainous city would carry the Chinese revolution to eventual victory.
Kong Xia's grandfather, Kong Xianquan, a Red Army staff officer, witnessed the great transformation. Storming the pass with his unit, the then 24-year-old was shot in the right leg. When he died in 1988, six pieces of shrapnel were found among his ashes.
His comrade, Zhong Chibing, badly wounded in the same battle, underwent three amputations without anesthetic as repeated infections set in under poor sanitary conditions. Rather than recuperate, the young man insisted on staying with the army and completed the Long March on one leg.
Their stories capture the resilience that defined Red Army soldiers: a refusal to let hardship stand in the way of the cause they believed in.
Born in 1911 to a peasant family in Liuyang, central China's Hunan Province, Kong Xianquan joined the revolution for a simple reason. He wanted enough food to eat. He also wanted to find an army that did not bully people like the KMT troops. So he joined a peasant armed force in 1928, and then in 1930, the Red Army.
In 1954, Kong Xianquan became the first curator of the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall. Despite his wounded leg, the veteran traveled across mountains and valleys, collecting more than 1,200 precious artifacts for the memorial.
"My grandfather spoke less, but when he told stories of the past, he was always excited," Kong Xia told Xinhua in an interview. "He never kept an account of his own deeds. What he cared about was how to record history, so that those who came after could truly see the road they had traveled."
Today, Kong Xia has taken up her grandfather's baton to tell Long March stories. Since 1993, she has given more than 1,000 voluntary lectures to over 50,000 listeners, and has trained hundreds of young docents. Now retired, she continues to find new ways to bring these stories to younger generations.
The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the Long March victory, also the start of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). The next five years will be a critical stage for the country to advance toward its goal of basically realizing socialist modernization by 2035.
Kong Xia believes the Long March spirit, which comes down to keeping the faith, braving setback after setback, and putting the people first, is important to achieving the Chinese dream. "When people tell the Long March stories today, they do not tell to dwell on misery, but to light the way forward," she said.
The Long March is never a story told merely within China. First published in Britain in 1937, American journalist Edgar Snow's "Red Star Over China" introduced the Chinese revolution to international readers. Decades later, Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Harrison Salisbury retraced the route and described the Long March as "a great human epic."
This year, Kong Xia has seen a growing number of foreign visitors at the memorial hall and other historical sites in Zunyi. She attributes the rise to China's prosperity and stability.
"They come with questions: Why did China succeed in the past? Will it continue to succeed? I believe there will be even more foreign visitors in the future. Because as other countries develop, China's experience may serve as a reference," she added.
Ninety years on, the Long March stories are still being told. And for Kong Xia, these stories are worth telling for a lifetime, and the spirit in the stories will keep traveling -- to new listeners, in new languages, and for years to come.

item.title: China's longest undersea highway tunnel completes shield tunneling
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Constructors make a safety inspection at the construction site of Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, Oct. 2, 2026. China's longest undersea highway tunnel completed all shield-driven excavation work on Friday as a shield machine reached its designated position at a depth of 105 meters beneath the sea surface in Jiaozhou Bay, eastern China's Shandong Province, according to China Railway Construction Corporation Limited. The Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Tunnel will connect Qingdao's main urban area with the Qingdao West Coast New Area. The latter is a national-level new area. The 17.48-km project includes a 14.37-km main tunnel section, featuring two main tunnels and a middle service tunnel, with three lanes in each direction and a design speed of 80 km per hour. (Xinhua/Li Ziheng)
BEIJING, Oct. 2 (Xinhua) -- China's longest undersea highway tunnel completed all shield-driven excavation work on Friday as a shield machine reached its designated position at a depth of 105 meters beneath the sea surface in Jiaozhou Bay, eastern China's Shandong Province, according to China Railway Construction Corporation Limited.
According to Wang Junping with the China Railway 14th Bureau Group Corporation Limited, the project used a combination of drill-and-blast and shield tunneling methods, advancing from both the east and west shores of Jiaozhou Bay and meeting under the sea.
The main shield section has a maximum depth of 95 meters below the sea surface, and the service tunnel reaches 105 meters, creating high water pressure and requiring stringent sealing and waterproofing.
The team, for the first time, adopted a new muck discharge system, integrating a screw conveyor, rock crusher box and rock crusher, to improve efficiency and reduce blockage risks, Wang said, adding that innovative anti-vibration technology was developed for the shield body to improve stability.
Once completed, the new tunnel will help Qingdao form a multi-level cross-bay transport network together with the existing Jiaozhou Bay Tunnel, Jiaozhou Bay Bridge and Jiaozhou Bay Highway.
China has issued a plan to comprehensively advance the high-quality development of integrated transport services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the Ministry of Transport announced in July this year. The plan aims to largely establish a modern integrated transport service system by 2030.
Under the plan, China will improve connections among different modes of transport, make passenger transfers more convenient and enhance freight logistics services. It will also promote the integration of transport and tourism, improve services at transport hubs, and strengthen rural passenger transport, freight and delivery services.

item.title: China's Shenzhou-23 astronauts send National Day greetings from space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
Chinese astronauts Zhu Yangzhu (C), Zhang Zhiyuan (R) and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, for the upcoming Shenzhou-23 crewed spaceflight mission, meet the press at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, May 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Lian Zhen)
BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-23 astronauts aboard China's Tiangong space station sent video greetings to their motherland on Thursday, which is China's National Day and the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
Commander Zhu Yangzhu and his crewmates Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered their wishes for the country and its space program together as the station, about 400 km above Earth, flew over China.
"When we look at Earth from the space station, that brilliantly lit land is the motherland we miss day and night," said Li, the first astronaut from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to travel to space.
The three astronauts were launched aboard the Shenzhou-23 spaceship late on May 24 and have been in orbit for more than four months. They are in good condition, having completed in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-21 astronauts, repaired the station's solar panels in a spacewalk and deployed application payloads outside the station.
This year marks the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program. Remarkable milestones include the launch of the country's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System that offers global services, the Chang'e lunar missions, the Tianwen-1 Mars mission, the Tiangong space station and the steady advance of crewed lunar exploration project.
"We can never forget that in deserts, mountains and on islands, a group of people have gazed at the stars and kept striving, generation after generation, for 70 years, creating the glory of China's space program," said Zhang, who is on his first spaceflight.
Zhu, from China's third batch of astronauts, is on his second spaceflight after the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, and is commanding a long-duration mission for the first time. "The 'baton of history' has been passed to us. We will certainly run this leg well, and keep safeguarding and building our home in space," he said.

item.title: Macao SAR celebrates National Day with flag-raising ceremony, reception
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
A flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China is held at the Golden Lotus Square in Macao, south China, October 1, 2026. /VCG
The government of China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on Thursday held a flag-raising ceremony and a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
The flag-raising ceremony took place at 8 a.m. at Macao's Golden Lotus Square. The national anthem was played, and China's national flag and the flag of the Macao SAR were hoisted.
The ceremony was followed by a reception hosted by the Macao SAR government at the China-Portuguese-speaking Countries Commercial and Trade Service Platform Complex.
Speaking at the event, Macao SAR Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai said the SAR government has proactively aligned with the country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), pooling wisdom and building consensus across all sectors to formulate and implement its own third five-year plan.
Looking ahead, the Macao SAR government will anchor its efforts on two key pillars – adopting refined governance with a "resident-centered" approach, as well as preventing and mitigating internal and external risks and challenges – thereby achieving sustainable development while effectively addressing these risks and challenges, Sam said.
He called for invigorating the market, enhancing the well-being of the people and striving to write a new chapter in the successful practice of "One Country, Two Systems" with Macao characteristics.

item.title: HKSAR gov't holds flag-raising ceremony, reception to celebrate National Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-02
The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a flag-raising ceremony to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo)
HONG KONG, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) on Thursday held a flag-raising ceremony and a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
The flag-raising ceremony was held at the Golden Bauhinia Square on Thursday morning. The national anthem was played, and China's national flag and the flag of the HKSAR were hoisted.
The ceremony was followed by a reception hosted by the HKSAR government in the adjoining Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center.
Noting that this is the first National Day celebrated since the announcement of Hong Kong's first five-year plan, HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee said at the reception that the plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong to seize the opportunities brought by national development by applying its unique advantages under "one country, two systems."
"I am confident that as long as we, each dedicated to our respective roles, join hands and work in synergy with one another, Hong Kong will certainly be able to set out on a path to a brighter and more prosperous future," said Lee.
The government of China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) holds a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo)
Helicopters carrying China's national flag and the flag of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) are seen in south China's Hong Kong, Oct. 1, 2026. item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.
China's National Day falls on Oct. 1.
Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests.
"The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China."
He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability.
"We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said.
Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said.
Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said.
Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy.
He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added.
He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification.
China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said.
The Communist Party of China and state leaders Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attend a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China along with around 800 guests at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, presides over a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)
